questions.stem: How can you demonstrate that living organisms produce carbon dioxide during respiration?

options.text: By using limewater or hydrogencarbonate indicator, which changes colour in the presence of CO2

questions.explanation: Limewater turns milky/cloudy when carbon dioxide is bubbled through it. Hydrogencarbonate indicator changes from orange to yellow as CO2 increases (becomes more acidic).

options.text: The rate of oxygen consumption or carbon dioxide production during respiration

questions.explanation: A respirometer measures the rate of respiration by tracking oxygen uptake or CO2 release. It typically uses a sealed container with an organism and measures gas volume changes.

questions.stem: Why is sodium hydroxide (or potassium hydroxide) used in a respirometer?

options.text: To absorb carbon dioxide produced by respiration, so only oxygen uptake is measured

questions.explanation: Sodium/potassium hydroxide absorbs the CO2 produced during respiration. This means any change in gas volume is due to oxygen consumption only, giving an accurate measure of oxygen uptake.

questions.stem: How can you show that germinating seeds respire faster than dormant seeds?

options.text: By using a respirometer to compare their rates of oxygen consumption

questions.explanation: A respirometer can compare rates of respiration. Germinating seeds, which are actively growing, will consume oxygen much faster than dormant (resting) seeds, shown by a faster change in gas volume.

questions.stem: What happens to the rate of respiration when temperature increases?

options.text: It increases up to an optimum, then decreases rapidly as enzymes denature

questions.explanation: Increasing temperature initially increases the rate of respiration as enzyme reactions speed up. Beyond the optimum temperature, respiratory enzymes denature and the rate drops rapidly.

questions.stem: Why is a control tube (with dead or no organisms) needed in a respiration experiment?

options.text: To make the experiment look complete
To show that any changes observed are due to respiration by the living organisms, not other factors

questions.explanation: A control tube shows that changes in gas volume or indicator colour are caused by the organism's respiration and not by other factors such as temperature changes or chemical reactions.

questions.stem: How can you show that respiration produces heat?

options.text: By placing a thermometer in a flask of germinating seeds and observing a temperature increase

questions.explanation: Germinating seeds placed in an insulated flask with a thermometer will show a rise in temperature over time, demonstrating that respiration is exothermic and releases heat energy.
